newsitem.title: JAPAN: DKB says has completely cut ties with racketeers.
newsitem.headline: DKB says has completely cut ties with racketeers.

text.p: The new president of scandal-hit Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd told its annual shareholders' meeting on Friday that the bank's new board of directors would have no ties with sokaiya corporate racketeers.
Katsuyuki Sugita, a managing director who was taking over as president after the meeting, said: "The new management will completely reject any requests from racketeers."

Katsuhiko Kondo, who was to step down as the bank's president after the meeting, said none of the 21 new directors approved at Friday's meeting had any involvement in a racketeer scandal that has rocked DKB, one of Japan's top commercial banks.
Kondo, who chaired the meeting, said according to the bank's internal investigation nobody (among the new directors) was involved in the case.
Kondo opened the meeting by saying the bank apologised for causing trouble to shareholders because bank executives had been arrested.
Explaining the payoff scandal, Kondo told shareholders that the bank still has 7.5 billion yen of loans outstanding to racketeers.
After Kondo's initial remarks, other comments by him and Sugita were made in response to questions from shareholders.

Asked if DKB planned to take legal action against former executives who have been arrested on suspicion of making payoffs to racketeers, Kondo said it was still unclear whether and how those former executives were involved in the alleged payoffs.
"We would like to come to a conclusion on this as soon as possible, also taking account of our internal investigation," Kondo said.
The meeting, which lasted about 90 minutes, ended without incident or any apparent attempt by sokaiya to interrupt it.
